definition: A COMPLETE dossier requires matchup-specific evidence, current market/model reconciliation, availability state, expert residual handling, invalidators and execution sensitivity. Schedule presence alone never qualifies.

mechanisms: Both offensive lines face elite opposing fronts; the most credible early-game path is suppressed efficient rushing and greater dependence on passing-game explosives.
Josh Pate specifically highlighted TE/personnel usage and elite WRs as the likely explosive-play escape valve when conventional run-game chunk gains are difficult.
Separate PFF Week 2 research adds QB pressure/efficiency context, making protection and response to pressure central rather than generic team-strength inputs.
dossiers.availability: Continue late-week OL/front-seven and secondary availability checks; no unverified absence is converted into points.
expertResidual: Josh Pate: total-under compatible game-shape discussion, but no Under wager inferred from the attributable clip.
Pate/Lewan/Compton later took Texas to cover in an attributable transcript-derived source; no spread price was exposed, so none is inferred.
Solid Verbal Week 2 preview is discovered and PROVISIONAL until analyst-specific pick evidence is recoverable.
dossiers.modelRelationship: Expert evidence is qualitative residual only and does not overwrite the quantitative fair.
invalidators: early explosive plays defeating the expected trench compression
market crossing materially away from the near-pick'em range
dossiers.execution: No official side/total without current executable price and Bet Activation Gate clearance.

mechanisms: Michigan enters without a strong positive offensive foundation from Week 1 and now faces a Brent Venables defense capable of stressing a young quarterback with simulated pressure and post-snap complexity.
Early stalled drives can amplify home-crowd pressure on Bryce Underwood rather than automatically creating a home-field advantage.
Oklahoma's Week 1 blowout is confirmation of ceiling but is deliberately not converted one-for-one into rating points.
dossiers.availability: Recheck Michigan offensive personnel and Oklahoma defensive availability before final snapshot.
expertResidual: Josh Pate: Michigan offensive-foundation concern versus Oklahoma's defense; no ATS wager inferred from that segment.
Taylor Lewan: explicit Michigan moneyline, 5-unit conviction.
Nathan Hurst/Rock M Nation: explicit Oklahoma -5.5 position, creating meaningful cross-family disagreement.
dossiers.modelRelationship: Current expert set contains direct disagreement and therefore lowers confidence rather than being counted as multiple confirmations.
invalidators: Oklahoma pressure fails to reach Underwood
dossiers.execution: Treat -5.5 as current reference; no official activation solely from expert disagreement.

mechanisms: Rutgers' quarterback state materially changed: AJ Surace is expected to start with Dylan Lonergan injured/emergency-only.
The QB change directly affects passing efficiency, sack/pressure exposure and turnover distribution; no manual point value is invented.
The independent football layer has shown Rutgers-side value relative to the market, but that diagnostic output remains separate from the governed production fair.
dossiers.availability: Lonergan/Surace status is a mandatory pre-kickoff recheck.
dossiers.expertResidual: No correlated-source repetition is treated as independent confirmation.
dossiers.modelRelationship: QB uncertainty is a confidence/veto input until late-week status stabilizes.

dossiers.execution: No official Rutgers/BC position until QB state and executable line/juice are reconciled.

mechanisms: Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey enters with a credible passing-upside path after a 300+ yard, four-TD opener, improving the underdog's ability to punish Alabama if game state stays compressed.

Josh Pate flagged Alabama's historical road-favorite volatility under Kalen DeBoer and the difficulty of this specific healthy, engaged Lexington environment, while explicitly cautioning that history does not define this year's team.

Alabama starting RG Michael Carroll was reported doubtful, adding continuity/protection risk for Keelon Russell's first true road start; this remains an availability interpretation rather than an automatic spread adjustment.
dossiers.availability: Mandatory final check on Michael Carroll, AK Dear, Jireh Edwards, Noah Rogers and Kentucky RT/secondary availability.
dossiers.expertResidual: Pate's favorite-risk framing is not converted into a Kentucky wager; Solid Verbal Week 2 evidence remains PROVISIONAL until analyst-specific selections are recovered.
dossiers.modelRelationship: Longshot Lab context and expert residual are separate from Bet Activation Gate v1.1.
invalidators: early Alabama explosives destroy game compression
dossiers.execution: Research candidate only; no Kentucky ATS/ML inferred.

market.spread: Utah roughly -11.5 to -13.5 across Week 2 observations

mechanisms: Arkansas' upset path is driven by KJ Jackson's experience/dual-threat ability plus explosive/turnover variance rather than a claim of down-to-down superiority.
The underdog price lengthened materially during the week, but a larger number alone is not treated as value.
Arkansas' poor red-zone/turnover execution in Week 1 is both the source of upside variance and the primary reason the profile is not promoted automatically.
dossiers.availability: Continue monitoring Arkansas DE Quincy Rhodes Jr., RB Cam Settles and any Utah QB/offensive-line availability changes.
dossiers.expertResidual: Longshot classification is research only and is not counted as an official betting signal.
dossiers.modelRelationship: Outside the primary Underdog Special spread band; governed separately in Longshot Upset Lab.
invalidators: Utah establishes efficient early-down offense with no turnover opportunities
price shortens without improvement in football evidence
dossiers.execution: No official ML/ATS wager without a separate governed value and execution-gate clearance.
